leads_to.evidence: Most graduates take the FE exam near graduation, then work about four years under a licensed engineer before taking the PE exam. Only licensed PEs can sign plans and take responsible charge of projects.

nearby_pair.evidence: There is no nearby pair for this major.

school_matters.evidence: Civil engineers move up by licensing, not by school name. An ABET-accredited degree and the FE exam make a graduate an Engineer-in-Training, and the PE license that lets them approve plans takes about four more years of supervised work.

who_is_counted.evidence: The biggest civil engineering programs sit in large public engineering colleges, such as NC State's, which calls itself one of the largest in the country. They admit first-year students into four-year ABET degrees, not working adults finishing a degree.

programs.evidence: USC is a highly selective private university in Los Angeles, and its engineering graduates are recruited by top employers in a high-paying state.
Cal Poly says most of its graduates take jobs in California, among the best-paying states for civil engineers.
San Jose State admits most applicants, and its graduates mostly work in the Silicon Valley area, one of the highest-paying labor markets for civil engineers.
The program has too few graduates in the earnings cohort to give a reliable figure.
VMI commissions more officers than any school outside the federal service academies, so many of its civil engineering graduates start as military officers, not as civilian engineers.
Graduates mostly work in Puerto Rico, where engineering wages are well below those in the states.
